does: Cooks food in liquid that is kept just below a boil, so that it turns tender without being knocked about.
how: Bring the liquid up to a boil, then turn the heat down at once.
Find the setting where a few bubbles break the surface now and then.
Leave the lid off or ajar, so that the heat does not build back up to a boil.
Look in from time to time, and top the pot up if food shows above the liquid.

cues.text: A bubble or a small cluster of them rising every moment or so, and a surface that shivers.
Near silence. A pot that rolls and rattles is boiling.

mistakes.mistake: Letting it boil, which toughens meat and turns a stock cloudy.
mistakes.fix: Turn the heat down, or move the pot half off the burner.

mistakes.mistake: Covering the pot tightly, so that it climbs to a boil unseen.

comes_after.why: A simmer is found by coming down from a boil, so a cook has to know a boil first.
